result.title: Frame Evidence:A Benchmark for Reference Frames and Visual Evidence in Multi-Image Spatial Reasoning
result.summary: A spatial answer depends on the reference frame specified in language and its supporting visual evidence. Item accuracy alone obscures whether correctness persists when either changes. We introduce Frame Evidence, a benchmark of 320 matched triplets and 960 Chinese multiple-choice questions from captured and rendered scenes. One family compares three grounded reference frames over fixed images. The other pairs image deletion annotated as insufficient with answer-preserving addition. Joint metrics require correct answers across all three frames and paired evidence variants. Across 20 configurations on 288 held-out questions, GPT three-shot reaches 50.00\% item accuracy, but the best three-frame group accuracy is 5/48 (10.42\%), reached by GPT two-shot. Few-shot prompting and task-specific adaptation improve item accuracy without consistently improving joint correctness. Input controls show where images support matched success, while repeated executions reveal answer instability beneath similar scores.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Frame Evidence 基准，基于 320 个匹配三元组与 960 道中文选择题，在多图空间推理中联合考察指称参考系与视觉证据的充分/必要关系，并报告 20 种配置下的项目准确率与三帧联合正确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其联合指标与「图像删除标注为不充分／答案保持的添加」配对设计，可供核查 VLM 推理是否真正依赖视觉证据、答案是否随参考系与证据变化而稳定，与研究兴趣中的视觉证据筛选、因果作用与评价问题直接相关。
